```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  path <- normalizePath(path, mustWork = TRUE)

  repeat {
    has_readme <- file.exists(file.path(path, "README.md"))
    has_r_directory <- dir.exists(file.path(path, "R"))

    if (has_readme && has_r_directory) {
      return(path)
    }

    parent <- dirname(path)
    if (identical(parent, path)) {
      stop("Could not locate the repository root.")
    }
    path <- parent
  }
}

repo_root <- find_repo_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo_root)

input_source <- match.arg(
  params$input_source,
  choices = c("frozen", "live")
)
simulation_source <- match.arg(
  params$simulation_source,
  choices = c("reference", "rerun")
)
allow_live_api <- isTRUE(params$allow_live_api)

if (input_source == "live" && simulation_source == "reference") {
  stop(
    "The saved reference simulations correspond to the frozen manuscript inputs. ",
    "Use simulation_source = 'rerun' when input_source = 'live'."
  )
}
if (input_source == "live" && !allow_live_api) {
  stop(
    "Live mode makes OpenAI API calls. Set allow_live_api = TRUE explicitly ",
    "after reviewing the expected API usage."
  )
}

nsamples <- as.numeric(params$nsamples)
if (simulation_source == "rerun" &&
    (length(nsamples) != 1L || !is.finite(nsamples) ||
     nsamples < 1 || nsamples != floor(nsamples))) {
  stop("nsamples must be one positive integer when simulation_source = 'rerun'.")
}
nsamples <- as.integer(nsamples)

source(file.path(repo_root, "R", "parse_params.R"))
source(file.path(repo_root, "R", "sojourn_times.R"))
source(file.path(repo_root, "R", "w.R"))
source(file.path(repo_root, "R", "natural_history_simulation_two_test.R"))
source(file.path(repo_root, "R", "lead_time_two_test.R"))

case_cancer <- "colorectal cancer"
case_population <- "female population"
natural_history_seed <- 2782005L
screening_seed <- 2782006L

is_missing_table_value <- function(x) {
  length(x) == 0L || is.na(x) || !nzchar(trimws(as.character(x))) ||
    toupper(trimws(as.character(x))) == "NA"
}

table_value <- function(parameter_table, quantity) {
  if (!all(c("Quantity", "Value") %in% names(parameter_table))) {
    stop("Each parameter table must contain Quantity and Value columns.")
  }

  location <- which(trimws(parameter_table$Quantity) == quantity)
  if (length(location) != 1L) {
    stop(
      "Expected exactly one row named '", quantity,
      "'; found ", length(location), "."
    )
  }

  parameter_table$Value[[location]]
}

numeric_table_value <- function(parameter_table, quantity) {
  value <- table_value(parameter_table, quantity)
  parsed <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))

  if (length(parsed) != 1L || !is.finite(parsed)) {
    stop("The value for '", quantity, "' must be one finite number.")
  }
  parsed
}

probability_table_value <- function(parameter_table, quantity) {
  value <- percent_to_prob(table_value(parameter_table, quantity))

  if (length(value) != 1L || !is.finite(value) || value < 0 || value > 1) {
    stop("The value for '", quantity, "' must be a probability in [0, 1].")
  }
  value
}

mst_table_value <- function(parameter_table) {
  age_specific <- table_value(parameter_table, "MST by age band (years)")

  if (!is_missing_table_value(age_specific)) {
    parsed <- parse_param_value(age_specific)
    if (!is.data.frame(parsed) || !all(c("age_band", "value") %in% names(parsed)) ||
        any(!is.finite(parsed$value)) || any(parsed$value <= 0)) {
      stop("The age-specific MST value could not be parsed.")
    }
    return(parsed)
  }

  single_mst <- table_value(
    parameter_table,
    "Recommended single MST for simulation (years)"
  )
  parsed <- parse_param_value(single_mst)
  if (!is.numeric(parsed) || length(parsed) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(parsed) || parsed <= 0) {
    stop("The recommended single MST must be one positive number.")
  }
  parsed
}

format_mst <- function(mst) {
  if (is.data.frame(mst)) {
    return(paste0(mst$age_band, ": ", mst$value, collapse = "; "))
  }
  format(mst, trim = TRUE)
}
```

# Purpose and choices

This vignette follows the complete case-study path from structured agent outputs
to the two-test natural-history and screening simulations. It makes the
composition of the two agentic templates explicit: Template 2 identifies two
tests and their screening schedules, and Template 1 is then applied separately
to each selected test to identify its mean sojourn time (MST), sensitivity, and
specificity.

The input and simulation sources must be selected **before rendering**:

1. `input_source = "frozen"` reads the three agent-generated tables selected for
   the manuscript. `input_source = "live"` makes three new agentic calls.
2. `simulation_source = "reference"` reads the saved manuscript simulation
   objects. `simulation_source = "rerun"` generates new natural-history and
   screening objects.
3. Live mode additionally requires `allow_live_api = TRUE` as an explicit
   confirmation that the rendering will make API calls.

The safe and reproducible default is `input_source = "frozen"` with
`simulation_source = "reference"`. Live calls require internet access, an
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, access to the configured OpenAI model, and sufficient API
credits. They are not deterministic. The live option cannot be combined with
the reference simulations, because those simulations were generated from the
frozen manuscript inputs.

The current rendering uses `input_source = "`r input_source`"` and
`simulation_source = "`r simulation_source`"`.

The three valid configurations are:

| `input_source` | `simulation_source` | `allow_live_api` | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"frozen"` | `"reference"` | `FALSE` | Read the manuscript tables and saved simulations |
| `"frozen"` | `"rerun"` | `FALSE` | Read the manuscript tables and run a new simulation |
| `"live"` | `"rerun"` | `TRUE` | Run three agentic workflows and a new simulation |

To retain multiple renderings, run the following block from the R console at
the repository root. Change only the four values under **Configuration**. Each
HTML file receives a timestamp and is saved under `vignettes/rendered/`, which
is ignored by Git.

```r
# Configuration
input_source <- "frozen"          # "frozen" or "live"
simulation_source <- "reference" # "reference" or "rerun"
allow_live_api <- FALSE           # TRUE is required for live mode
nsamples <- 1000000L              # Used only when rerunning

# Render and retain this run
render_directory <- file.path("vignettes", "rendered")
dir.create(render_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

run_timestamp <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
output_filename <- sprintf(
  "whole_workflow_%s_%s_%s.html",
  input_source,
  simulation_source,
  run_timestamp
)

rmarkdown::render(
  "vignettes/whole_workflow.Rmd",
  output_file = output_filename,
  output_dir = render_directory,
  params = list(
    input_source = input_source,
    simulation_source = simulation_source,
    allow_live_api = allow_live_api,
    nsamples = nsamples
  ),
  envir = new.env(parent = globalenv())
)
```

Alternatively, RStudio's **Knit with Parameters** interface can configure an
individual rendering, but the console block above is preferable when retaining
several named records.

The two paths connect as follows:

```text
Live path                              Frozen path

Template 2                             Saved Template 2 table
    |                                           |
    v                                           v
Test 1 and Test 2                      Test 1 and Test 2
    |                                           |
    v                                           v
Template 1 for each test               Two saved Template 1 tables
               \                         /
                \                       /
                 v                     v
                 Parsed simulation inputs
                            |
                            v
                  Penetrance input + model
                            |
                            v
                Natural-history simulation
                            |
                            v
                   Screening simulation
                            |
                            v
                  Summaries and selected plots
```

# Obtain the structured agent outputs

## Frozen manuscript inputs

This path reads the complete structured tables selected for the manuscript. It
does not call the OpenAI API.

```{r frozen-agent-inputs, eval=params$input_source == "frozen"}
if (input_source != "frozen") {
  stop("This chunk is only for input_source = 'frozen'.")
}

agent_input_dir <- file.path(
  "data", "paper_case_study", "agent_generated_inputs"
)

screening_strategy <- read.csv(
  file.path(agent_input_dir, "parameters_20260819_154630.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)
test1_parameters <- read.csv(
  file.path(agent_input_dir, "parameters_20260814_195949.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)
test2_parameters <- read.csv(
  file.path(agent_input_dir, "parameters_20260814_190648.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

## Live agent calls

This path first invokes Template 2. The two returned test names are then used to
construct two separate Template 1 requests. The resulting tables are written to
`logs/` by the agentic workflow and are also retained in this R session.

```{r live-agent-inputs, eval=params$input_source == "live"}
if (input_source != "live" || !allow_live_api) {
  stop(
    "This chunk makes live API calls. Select input_source = 'live' and set ",
    "allow_live_api = TRUE before running it."
  )
}

source(file.path("R", "run_agentic_parameters.R"))

strategy_problem <- paste(
  "For", case_cancer, "in the", case_population,
  "identify two clinically relevant asymptomatic screening tests consistent",
  "with the monotonic two-test model, and propose one literature-grounded",
  "candidate screening strategy for each test, consisting of a screening",
  "start age, stop age, and fixed interval."
)

strategy_run <- run_agentic_parameters(
  problem_text = strategy_problem,
  template = "two_test_model"
)
screening_strategy <- strategy_run$parameters

selected_test1 <- table_value(screening_strategy, "Test 1 name")
selected_test2 <- table_value(screening_strategy, "Test 2 name")

test1_problem <- sprintf(
  "Estimate parameters for %s screening with %s in the %s.",
  case_cancer, selected_test1, case_population
)
test2_problem <- sprintf(
  "Estimate parameters for %s screening with %s in the %s.",
  case_cancer, selected_test2, case_population
)

test1_run <- run_agentic_parameters(
  problem_text = test1_problem,
  template = "one_test_model"
)
test2_run <- run_agentic_parameters(
  problem_text = test2_problem,
  template = "one_test_model"
)

test1_parameters <- test1_run$parameters
test2_parameters <- test2_run$parameters
```

The three structured tables should be reviewed before their values are treated
as candidate simulation inputs. For compactness, the vignette displays their
quantities and values below; the saved CSV files retain the evidence, sources,
notes, and number of Proposer--Critic rounds.

```{r display-agent-inputs}
knitr::kable(
  screening_strategy[c("Quantity", "Value")],
  caption = "Template 2: selected tests and screening schedules"
)

knitr::kable(
  test1_parameters[c("Quantity", "Value")],
  caption = "Template 1: Test 1 parameters"
)

knitr::kable(
  test2_parameters[c("Quantity", "Value")],
  caption = "Template 1: Test 2 parameters"
)
```

# Construct the simulation inputs

The table rows are now converted into the arguments expected by the two-test
simulation functions. An age-specific MST is used when it is available;
otherwise, the recommended single MST is used.

```{r parse-agent-inputs}
test1_name <- as.character(table_value(screening_strategy, "Test 1 name"))
age_min1 <- numeric_table_value(
  screening_strategy,
  "Test 1 screening start age (years)"
)
age_max1 <- numeric_table_value(
  screening_strategy,
  "Test 1 screening stop age (years)"
)
Delta_t1 <- numeric_table_value(
  screening_strategy,
  "Test 1 screening interval (years)"
)

test2_name <- as.character(table_value(screening_strategy, "Test 2 name"))
age_min2 <- numeric_table_value(
  screening_strategy,
  "Test 2 screening start age (years)"
)
age_max2 <- numeric_table_value(
  screening_strategy,
  "Test 2 screening stop age (years)"
)
Delta_t2 <- numeric_table_value(
  screening_strategy,
  "Test 2 screening interval (years)"
)

MST1 <- mst_table_value(test1_parameters)
sensitivity1 <- probability_table_value(test1_parameters, "Sensitivity")
specificity1 <- probability_table_value(test1_parameters, "Specificity")

MST2 <- mst_table_value(test2_parameters)
sensitivity2 <- probability_table_value(test2_parameters, "Sensitivity")
specificity2 <- probability_table_value(test2_parameters, "Specificity")

simulation_inputs <- data.frame(
  test = c("Test 1", "Test 2"),
  name = c(test1_name, test2_name),
  screening_start_age = c(age_min1, age_min2),
  screening_stop_age = c(age_max1, age_max2),
  screening_interval = c(Delta_t1, Delta_t2),
  MST = c(format_mst(MST1), format_mst(MST2)),
  sensitivity = c(sensitivity1, sensitivity2),
  specificity = c(specificity1, specificity2),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  simulation_inputs,
  caption = "Parsed inputs for the two-test simulation"
)
```

The natural-history simulation additionally requires an age-specific
penetrance vector. The repository includes the vector used in the manuscript
case study, so the full example does not require access to the private
`Fam3PRODatabase`.

```{r penetrance-input}
penetrance_data <- read.csv(
  file.path(
    "data", "paper_case_study", "simulation_inputs",
    "colorectal_female_seer_net_penetrance.csv"
  )
)

stopifnot(
  identical(penetrance_data$age, seq_len(nrow(penetrance_data))),
  all(is.finite(penetrance_data$penetrance)),
  all(penetrance_data$penetrance >= 0),
  all(penetrance_data$penetrance <= 1)
)

penetrance <- penetrance_data$penetrance

knitr::kable(
  rbind(head(penetrance_data, 3), tail(penetrance_data, 3)),
  caption = "First and last three rows of the case-study penetrance input",
  digits = 9
)
```

# Obtain the simulation results

## Read the reference simulation

The reference path loads the natural-history and screening objects used for the
reported manuscript results. This avoids rerunning the million-history
simulation.

```{r reference-simulation, eval=params$simulation_source == "reference"}
if (simulation_source != "reference") {
  stop("This chunk is only for simulation_source = 'reference'.")
}

reference_output_dir <- file.path(
  "data", "paper_case_study", "reference_outputs"
)

natural_history <- readRDS(
  file.path(reference_output_dir, "natural_history.rds")
)
lead_time_results <- readRDS(
  file.path(reference_output_dir, "lead_time.rds")
)
```

## Rerun the simulation

The rerun path uses the parsed inputs and fixed manuscript seeds. With
`nsamples = 1000000` and the frozen parameter tables, it reproduces the saved
reference objects. Smaller values of `nsamples` are useful for demonstrating
the workflow but do not reproduce the reported numerical results.

```{r rerun-simulation, eval=params$simulation_source == "rerun"}
if (simulation_source != "rerun") {
  stop("This chunk is only for simulation_source = 'rerun'.")
}

if (nsamples != 1000000L) {
  message(
    "This rendering uses ", format(nsamples, big.mark = ","),
    " histories and is therefore a demonstration, not a reproduction of ",
    "the reported million-history simulation."
  )
}

set.seed(natural_history_seed)
natural_history <- natural_history_simulation_two_test(
  cancer = "Colorectal",
  gene = "SEER",
  sex = "Female",
  MST1 = MST1,
  MST2 = MST2,
  penetrance = penetrance,
  nsamples = nsamples,
  verbose = FALSE
)

lead_time_results <- lead_time_two_test(
  natural_history = natural_history,
  sensitivity1 = sensitivity1,
  specificity1 = specificity1,
  age_min1 = age_min1,
  age_max1 = age_max1,
  Delta_t1 = Delta_t1,
  sensitivity2 = sensitivity2,
  specificity2 = specificity2,
  age_min2 = age_min2,
  age_max2 = age_max2,
  Delta_t2 = Delta_t2,
  seed = screening_seed,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

# Principal results

The natural-history denominators and screening denominators are different.
Transition counts refer to all simulated histories. Screen detection and lead
time are evaluated only for histories with a modeled clinical-diagnosis age,
whereas false-positive results are evaluated across all simulated histories.

```{r principal-results}
n_histories <- length(natural_history$age1)
n_reaching_sp2 <- sum(!is.na(natural_history$age2_1))
n_reaching_sc <- sum(!is.na(natural_history$age2_2))

screen_detected <- lead_time_results$screen_detected %in% TRUE
n_screen_detected <- sum(screen_detected)
detection_fraction <- n_screen_detected / n_reaching_sc

detected_lead_time <- lead_time_results$lead_time[screen_detected]
mean_lead_time <- mean(detected_lead_time)

total_false_positives <- sum(lead_time_results$n_false_positives)
n_with_false_positive <- sum(lead_time_results$n_false_positives > 0)
false_positive_fraction <- n_with_false_positive / n_histories

principal_results <- data.frame(
  measure = c(
    "Simulated histories",
    "Histories reaching Sp2",
    "Histories reaching Sc by the modeled age limit",
    "Histories detected through screening",
    "Screen-detected fraction among histories reaching Sc",
    "Mean lead time among screen-detected histories (years)",
    "False-positive results",
    "Histories with at least one false-positive result",
    "Fraction with at least one false-positive result"
  ),
  value = c(
    format(n_histories, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(n_reaching_sp2, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(n_reaching_sc, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(n_screen_detected, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * detection_fraction),
    sprintf("%.2f", mean_lead_time),
    format(total_false_positives, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(n_with_false_positive, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * false_positive_fraction)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  principal_results,
  col.names = c("Measure", "Value"),
  caption = "Principal natural-history and screening results"
)
```

For the frozen reference path, the following checks guard against accidental
replacement or modification of the saved case-study objects.

```{r reference-checks, eval=params$input_source == "frozen" && params$simulation_source == "reference"}
if (input_source != "frozen" || simulation_source != "reference") {
  stop("These checks apply only to the frozen/reference path.")
}

stopifnot(
  n_histories == 1000000L,
  n_reaching_sp2 == 876840L,
  n_reaching_sc == 826660L,
  n_screen_detected == 252776L,
  total_false_positives == 800292L,
  n_with_false_positive == 536309L,
  isTRUE(all.equal(mean_lead_time, 3.773258, tolerance = 1e-6))
)
```

# Selected plots

The plots below preserve the binning, count or density scale, colors, axis
formatting, and font scaling used for the manuscript figures. With the frozen
reference objects, they reproduce the manuscript plots. The same plotting code
is applied to newly simulated objects in either rerun mode. The figures are
generated directly in this vignette; no separate plotting script is required.

```{r paper-plot-objects, include=FALSE}
paper_grey <- rgb(0.55, 0.55, 0.55, 0.6)
paper_blue <- rgb(0.30, 0.47, 0.66, 0.7)
paper_red <- rgb(0.72, 0.32, 0.32, 0.7)
paper_border <- "grey70"
paper_line <- "grey35"
paper_cex_lab <- 3.3
paper_cex_axis <- 2.7
paper_cex_legend <- 2.8

age_sp1 <- natural_history$age1
age_sp2 <- natural_history$age2_1
age_sc <- natural_history$age2_2

n_age_sp1 <- sum(!is.na(age_sp1))
n_age_sp2 <- sum(!is.na(age_sp2))
n_age_sc <- sum(!is.na(age_sc))

duration_t12 <- age_sp2 - age_sp1
duration_t2 <- age_sc - age_sp2

hist_age_sp1 <- hist(age_sp1, plot = FALSE, breaks = seq(0, 95, by = 5))
hist_age_sp2 <- hist(age_sp2, plot = FALSE, breaks = seq(0, 95, by = 5))
hist_age_sc <- hist(age_sc, plot = FALSE, breaks = seq(0, 95, by = 5))
hist_duration_t12 <- hist(
  duration_t12,
  plot = FALSE,
  breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 0.5)
)
hist_duration_t2 <- hist(
  duration_t2,
  plot = FALSE,
  breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 0.5)
)

transition_ylim <- c(0, max(hist_age_sp1$counts)) * 1.1
transition_ticks <- if (n_histories == 1000000L) {
  seq(0, 150000, length.out = 3)
} else {
  pretty(transition_ylim, n = 3)
}

plot_transition_age <- function(histogram, x_label, n) {
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par), add = TRUE)
  par(mar = c(5.5, 6.7, 2, 2) + 0.1)
  par(mgp = c(4.5, 1.5, 0))

  plot(
    histogram,
    xlab = x_label,
    ylab = "Counts",
    main = NULL,
    col = paper_grey,
    border = paper_border,
    cex.lab = paper_cex_lab,
    cex.axis = paper_cex_axis,
    yaxt = "n",
    ylim = transition_ylim
  )
  axis(
    2,
    at = transition_ticks,
    labels = formatC(transition_ticks, format = "e", digits = 1),
    cex.axis = paper_cex_axis
  )
  legend(
    "topleft",
    paste0("N = ", n),
    bty = "n",
    cex = paper_cex_lab
  )
}

plot_duration_density <- function(histogram, x_label) {
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par), add = TRUE)
  par(mar = c(6.5, 7.5, 2, 2) + 0.1)
  par(mgp = c(4.5, 1.5, 0))

  plot(
    histogram$mids,
    histogram$density,
    xlab = x_label,
    ylab = "Density",
    main = NULL,
    col = paper_line,
    type = "l",
    cex.lab = paper_cex_lab,
    cex.axis = paper_cex_axis,
    lwd = 5
  )
}

paper_lead_times <- lead_time_results$lead_time
paper_lead_times <- paper_lead_times[
  !is.na(paper_lead_times) & paper_lead_times > 0
]

test1_administrations <-
  lead_time_results$n_test1_before_true_positive[screen_detected]
test2_administrations <-
  lead_time_results$n_test2_before_true_positive[screen_detected]

plot_administrations <- function(x, test_number, color) {
  administration_table <- table(x)
  administration_values <- as.integer(names(administration_table))
  administration_ylim <- c(0, max(administration_table) * 1.1)

  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par), add = TRUE)
  par(mar = c(6.5, 7.8, 1.5, 1.5) + 0.1)
  par(mgp = c(4.7, 1.5, 0))

  bar_midpoints <- barplot(
    administration_table,
    xlab = paste("Test", test_number, "administrations"),
    ylab = "Counts",
    main = NULL,
    col = color,
    names.arg = rep("", length(administration_table)),
    border = paper_border,
    cex.lab = paper_cex_lab,
    cex.axis = paper_cex_axis,
    yaxt = "n",
    ylim = administration_ylim
  )

  labels_to_show <- if (length(administration_values) <= 12L) {
    seq_along(administration_values)
  } else {
    which(
      administration_values %% 5L == 0L |
        administration_values == max(administration_values)
    )
  }
  axis(
    1,
    at = bar_midpoints[labels_to_show],
    labels = administration_values[labels_to_show],
    cex.axis = paper_cex_axis
  )

  administration_ticks <- pretty(administration_ylim, n = 3)
  axis(
    2,
    at = administration_ticks,
    labels = formatC(administration_ticks, format = "e", digits = 1),
    cex.axis = paper_cex_axis
  )
}
```

## Natural-history transition ages and state durations

The transition-age plots use all histories reaching the corresponding state.
The duration plots show time in `Sp1` among histories reaching `Sp2` and time in
`Sp2` among histories reaching `Sc`.

```{r age-sp1-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=11, out.width="55%", fig.align="center"}
plot_transition_age(
  hist_age_sp1,
  expression(S[p1] * " Transition age (yr)"),
  n_age_sp1
)
```

```{r age-sp2-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=11, out.width="55%", fig.align="center"}
plot_transition_age(
  hist_age_sp2,
  expression(S[p2] * " Transition age (yr)"),
  n_age_sp2
)
```

```{r age-sc-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=11, out.width="55%", fig.align="center"}
plot_transition_age(
  hist_age_sc,
  expression(S[c] * " Transition age (yr)"),
  n_age_sc
)
```

```{r duration-sp1-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, out.width="55%", fig.align="center"}
plot_duration_density(
  hist_duration_t12,
  expression("Duration in " * S[p1] * (yr))
)
```

```{r duration-sp2-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, out.width="55%", fig.align="center"}
plot_duration_density(

  expression("Duration in " * S[p2] * (yr))
)
```

## Lead time

Lead time is plotted among screen-detected histories with positive lead time.
Interval cases and histories without a modeled clinical age are not included.

```{r lead-time-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=11, out.width="65%", fig.align="center"}
hist_lead_time <- hist(paper_lead_times, plot = FALSE)
lead_time_ylim <- c(0, max(hist_lead_time$counts) * 1.1)
lead_time_ticks <- pretty(lead_time_ylim, n = 3)

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mar = c(6.5, 7.8, 1.5, 1.5) + 0.1)
par(mgp = c(4.7, 1.5, 0))

plot(
  hist_lead_time,
  xlab = "Lead time (yr)",
  ylab = "Counts",
  main = NULL,
  col = paper_grey,
  border = paper_border,
  cex.lab = paper_cex_lab,
  cex.axis = paper_cex_axis,
  yaxt = "n",
  ylim = lead_time_ylim
)
axis(
  2,
  at = lead_time_ticks,
  labels = formatC(lead_time_ticks, format = "e", digits = 1),
  cex.axis = paper_cex_axis
)

par(old_par)
```

## False-positive results

False-positive counts are evaluated across all simulated histories. The
combined count is the per-history sum for the two tests.

```{r false-positive-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=11, out.width="65%", fig.align="center"}
n_test1_false_positives <- lead_time_results$n_test1_false_positives
n_test2_false_positives <- lead_time_results$n_test2_false_positives
n_false_positives <- lead_time_results$n_false_positives
known_false_positives <- !is.na(n_false_positives)
max_false_positives <- max(n_false_positives, na.rm = TRUE)

false_positive_counts <- rbind(
  "Test 1" = tabulate(
    n_test1_false_positives[known_false_positives] + 1L,
    nbins = max_false_positives + 1L
  ),
  "Test 2" = tabulate(
    n_test2_false_positives[known_false_positives] + 1L,
    nbins = max_false_positives + 1L
  ),
  "Combined" = tabulate(
    n_false_positives[known_false_positives] + 1L,
    nbins = max_false_positives + 1L
  )
)

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mar = c(6.5, 7.8, 1.5, 1.5) + 0.1)
par(mgp = c(4.7, 1.5, 0))

bar_midpoints <- barplot(
  false_positive_counts,
  beside = TRUE,
  xlab = "False-positive results per history",
  ylab = "Histories",
  main = NULL,
  col = c(paper_blue, paper_red, paper_grey),
  names.arg = rep("", max_false_positives + 1L),
  border = paper_border,
  cex.lab = paper_cex_lab,
  cex.axis = paper_cex_axis,
  yaxt = "n"
)
axis(
  1,
  at = colMeans(bar_midpoints),
  labels = 0:max_false_positives,
  cex.axis = paper_cex_axis
)
false_positive_ticks <- pretty(
  c(0, max(false_positive_counts)),
  n = 3
)
axis(
  2,
  at = false_positive_ticks,
  labels = formatC(false_positive_ticks, format = "e", digits = 1),
  cex.axis = paper_cex_axis
)
legend(
  "topright",
  legend = rownames(false_positive_counts),
  fill = c(paper_blue, paper_red, paper_grey),
  border = paper_border,
  bty = "n",
  cex = paper_cex_legend
)

par(old_par)
```

## Test administrations before screening detection

These plots include screen-detected histories only. They count administrations
strictly before the first positive screening detection by either test; an
administration at the detection age is not counted.

```{r test1-administration-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=11, out.width="65%", fig.align="center"}
plot_administrations(test1_administrations, 1, paper_blue)
```

```{r test2-administration-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=11, out.width="65%", fig.align="center"}
plot_administrations(test2_administrations, 2, paper_red)
```

# Reproducibility information

The reported case study used seed `r natural_history_seed` for natural history
and seed `r screening_seed` for screening. New live agent calls may yield
different tests, schedules, evidence, or parameter estimates even when the same
prompts are used. For reproducible analyses, retain the selected structured
tables and use them as frozen inputs.

```{r session-information}
sessionInfo()
```

The Python dependencies are needed only for live agent calls. Their installed
versions can be recorded with:

```{bash python-versions, eval=FALSE}
python3 --version
python3 -m pip show openai pandas striprtf
```

This is research software. The agent-generated strategies and parameters and
the resulting simulations require source verification and scientific and
clinical review; they are not clinical recommendations.
